suggestions.rationale: Adrenal histoplasmosis can produce primary adrenal insufficiency (Addison disease) when Histoplasma infection directly involves and damages the adrenal glands. A retrospective cohort of 40 adults with biopsy- or culture-supported adrenal histoplasmosis found primary adrenal insufficiency in 73% at presentation, with additional patients developing adrenal insufficiency during follow-up. This supports a disease-progression pathway only when adrenal or disseminated histoplasmosis is documented and endocrine testing confirms primary adrenal insufficiency; the broader catalog identity must not be used to infer Addison disease from pulmonary-only histoplasmosis or from nonspecific fatigue, weight loss, hypotension, or electrolyte abnormalities without adrenal disease and biochemical confirmation.

pathwayIntelligence.causalChain: Documented adrenal/disseminated histoplasmosis with adrenal involvement → adrenal cortical injury or loss of reserve → biochemically confirmed primary adrenal insufficiency / Addison disease.
developmentQuestions: Is adrenal involvement by histoplasmosis documented by imaging plus histology, culture, antigen testing, or other clinically accepted evidence rather than inferred from pulmonary histoplasmosis alone?
Do ACTH, morning cortisol, ACTH-stimulation testing, renin/aldosterone, sodium, and potassium findings support primary adrenal insufficiency?
Did adrenal insufficiency begin during or after the documented adrenal/disseminated histoplasmosis course?
Are bilateral adrenal enlargement, destructive adrenal changes, or other compatible adrenal findings documented?
Which competing causes of primary adrenal insufficiency, including autoimmune adrenalitis, hemorrhage, metastatic disease, tuberculosis, medication effects, or other infections, should be addressed?
issuesToResolve: The catalog identity includes pulmonary histoplasmosis, but pulmonary disease alone does not establish an adrenal pathway; adrenal or disseminated involvement must be documented.
Symptoms such as fatigue, weight loss, hypotension, and electrolyte abnormalities are not substitutes for biochemical confirmation of primary adrenal insufficiency.

evidenceGaps: Records establishing adrenal or disseminated histoplasmosis and the diagnostic method
Adrenal imaging and pathology/microbiology where available
Endocrine testing confirming primary adrenal insufficiency
Chronology of histoplasmosis, adrenal involvement, and adrenal-insufficiency onset
Endocrinology or infectious-disease assessment addressing competing adrenal etiologies

sourceReferences.citation: Singh M, Chandy DD, Bharani T, et al. Clinical outcomes and cortical reserve in adrenal histoplasmosis-A retrospective follow-up study of 40 patients. Clin Endocrinol (Oxf). 2019;90(4):534-541. PMID 30656706
sourceReferences.note: Retrospective cohort of 40 consecutive adults with adrenal histoplasmosis diagnosed by bilateral adrenal enlargement plus histology and/or culture found primary adrenal insufficiency in 73% at presentation; two initially eucortisolemic patients developed adrenal insufficiency during follow-up. Supports an adrenal-histoplasmosis-to-primary-adrenal-insufficiency pathway, not attribution from pulmonary-only histoplasmosis.
